# Configuration

pmsbridge is configured with environment variables. You set them in a file named `.env` next to
`deploy/compose.yaml`; the installer creates that file for you. The application reads nothing else:
there is no other configuration file and no web page for these settings. Never commit the `.env`
file or share it, because later versions keep secrets in it.

After you change `.env`, restart the stack so the change takes effect:

```
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml up -d
```

If a setting is wrong, the application stops at start-up and the logs name the setting and say what
is wrong. Look at them with `docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml logs app`.

## Application settings

In production (the default), `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` must start with `https://` and its host must be
exactly `DOMAIN`. With `ENVIRONMENT=development`, both may be left out and default to a local
address.

| Variable | Type | Default | Required in production | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ENVIRONMENT` | one of `production`, `development` | `production` | no | `production` requires HTTPS and a public address that matches `DOMAIN`. `development` relaxes those checks for running on your own machine. |
| `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | text | none (development: `http://localhost:8000`) | yes | The full public address of this installation, for example `https://mcp.example.com`. In production it must start with `https://` and its host must equal `DOMAIN`. |
| `DOMAIN` | text | none (development: `localhost`) | yes | The host name people use to reach this installation, for example `mcp.example.com`. |
| `DATA_DIR` | path | `/data` | no | The folder for everything the application stores. In the container it is a volume. |
| `DATABASE_PATH` | path | `<DATA_DIR>/pmsbridge.db` | no | The SQLite database file. |
| `BACKUP_DIR` | path | `<DATA_DIR>/backups` | no | The folder for automatic backups taken before a database upgrade. |
| `PRE_MIGRATION_BACKUPS_KEEP` | whole number | `5` | no | How many automatic pre-upgrade backups to keep. Older ones are deleted. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | one of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL` | `INFO` | no | How much detail goes to the logs. Logs never contain passwords, tokens or guest details. |

## Stack settings

These are read by the Docker Compose stack and Caddy, not by the application itself. `DOMAIN`
(above) is read by both.

| Variable | Default | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TLS_MODE` | `auto` | no | `auto` gets a real certificate for your domain. `internal` is for testing only. See [TLS and domains](tls-and-domains.md). |
| `ACME_EMAIL` | none | yes, when `TLS_MODE=auto` | An address the certificate authority can contact about your certificate. |
| `ACME_CA` | `production` | no | `production` or `staging`. Use `staging` only while experimenting, to avoid certificate limits. |
| `HTTP_PORT` | `80` | no | The server port that receives plain `http://` visits (they are redirected to HTTPS). Change it only for testing. |
| `HTTPS_PORT` | `443` | no | The server port that receives `https://` visits. Change it only for testing. |
| `TRUSTED_PROXIES` | Caddy's address on the private network | no | The addresses the application believes when they say who the visitor is. Leave it alone unless you know why you need to change it. |
| `BACKEND_SUBNET` | `172.31.250.0/24` | no | The private network between Caddy and the application. Change it only if it clashes with a network you use. |
| `CADDY_BACKEND_IP` | `172.31.250.10` | no | Caddy's fixed address on that private network. It must lie inside `BACKEND_SUBNET`. |
| `PMSBRIDGE_IMAGE` | `pmsbridge:local` | no | Which application image to run. The installer and the update command set this. |
| `PMSBRIDGE_CADDY_IMAGE` | `pmsbridge-caddy:local` | no | Which Caddy image to run. The installer and the update command set this. |
| `PMSBRIDGE_ENV_FILE` | `.env` | no | The settings file passed to the application. Only automated tests change it. |

## If the application stops after an update

When the application is updated, it upgrades its database when it starts. If that cannot be done,
the application stops and the container restarts again and again (`docker compose -f
deploy/compose.yaml ps` shows it restarting). Nothing is lost: the upgrade is rolled back, so the
database is left exactly as it was, and the log (`docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml logs app`)
says what went wrong. A message saying the database was created by a newer version means you started
an older version than the one that last ran.

The way out is to go back to the previous version of pmsbridge and start it. If you need to restore
the data as well, use the backup the application took just before the upgrade. Backups are in
`BACKUP_DIR` (`/data/backups` in the container) and are named `pre-migration-<date and
time>-<number>-from-<version>.db`. The newest one is the one taken for the failed upgrade. To
restore one:

1. Stop the stack: `docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml stop`.

2. With the stack stopped, copy the backup over the database file (use the real file name from
`/data/backups`):

```
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint sh app \
  -c 'cp /data/backups/BACKUP_FILE /data/pmsbridge.db \
      && rm -f /data/pmsbridge.db-wal /data/pmsbridge.db-shm'
```

3. Make sure the previous version of pmsbridge is the one that will start, then run `docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml up -d`.

## Where data is stored

Inside the container everything lives under `DATA_DIR` (`/data`), which is a Docker volume, so it
survives restarts and updates. The database file and the backups are readable only by the
application's own user. Before each database upgrade the application takes a backup of the database
into `BACKUP_DIR` and keeps the newest `PRE_MIGRATION_BACKUPS_KEEP` of them.
